value.name: confirm mutual understanding
value.description: A brief exchange confirms that both speakers understand what is being discussed.

value.name: ask about the older child
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks Asha about the older child in the household.

value.name: assess Daniel's fear
value.description: Asha observes Daniel and explains that he has been frightened for a long time and may soon improve or worsen.
evidence: Through the parlor doorway she could see the corner of the dining room table, the edge of Daniel's sleeve, the back of one of the chairs.
"He's frightened," she said. "He's been frightened for a long time and he didn't know it. He'll be difficult for a week and then he'll be either better or much worse, and I don't yet know which."

value.name: ask about the younger child
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks Asha about the younger child.

value.name: reflect on Lucia's vindication
value.description: Asha reflects that Lucia was right all along, had to be right alone, and now does not know how to handle being proven right aloud.
evidence: "She was right. She knew she was right. She had to be right alone in a house with people who told her she wasn't, for months, and now she gets to be right out loud, and she doesn't know what to do with that either."

value.name: insist she is fine
value.description: Asha insists that she is fine when Mr. Halloran asks about her.

value.name: receive counsel from Halloran
value.description: Mr. Halloran praises Asha as a good attorney, warns her not to confuse being moved with being compromised, and tells her to come in when she is done.
evidence: "You're a good attorney," he said, "and you have one bad habit, which is that you mistake being moved for being compromised. They are not the same thing. Let yourself be moved. Don't let yourself be retained twice. Come in when you're done."

value.name: end the phone call
value.description: Mr. Halloran hangs up, ending the conversation.

value.name: stand in the window and look outside
value.description: Asha sets down the phone and stands at the bay window, looking out at the street and its passersby.
evidence: She set the phone down on the parlor's marble-topped table and stood for a moment in the bay window looking out at the street.
A delivery truck idled at the curb three doors down. A woman with a stroller was negotiating the broken brick of the sidewalk.
